messages:
sara: quick planning check — we have a handful of customer asks around inference perf. primary ask: reduce tail latency for chat without tanking throughput or blowing up cost. i want to prioritize work for the next roadmap sprint (canary -> GA). thoughts on framework (RICE / impact vs effort) and concrete launch criteria?
cheng: can we get concrete KPIs? p50/p95 target, tokens/sec, budget delta? otherwise RICE scores will be useless :slightly_frowning_face:
miguel: telemetry snapshot: p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 1.2s for 1k-token chats during peak. throughput (tokens/s) across pools is fine, but tail spikes correlate with small-batch noisy inputs and KV-cache misses.
anya: quality note — heavy quantization or aggressive token pruning can change output distribution. any perf change needs prompt-set evals. i can run a focused eval (1000 prompts) but need storybook of customer prompts.
dana: customers we spoke to (enterprise subset) said predictable tail matters more than 5% cost cut. they'd pay for dedicated capacity to hit tail SLOs. so market impact probably high for latency fixes. :+1:
cheng: propose quick RICE sketch to compare three candidate initiatives: (A) KV prefix caching + cache-aware routing, (B) prioritized small-batch fast-path + micro-queueing, (C) quantization+compiler tweaks.
cheng: codeblock: `
# candidate, Reach(0-10), Impact(0-10), Confidence(0-10), Effort(mo)
A KV-cache, 7, 8, 7, 1.5
B small-batch path, 6, 9, 6, 2.5
C quant+kernels, 8, 6, 5, 3.0
`
cheng: rough RICE calc (R*I*C)/E -> A: (7*8*7)/1.5 ~ 261, B: (6*9*6)/2.5 ~ 130, C: (8*6*5)/3 ~ 80 — so KV-cache looks highest ROI.
sara: interesting — KV-cache is lower effort and good reach. but note cache adds infra ops complexity and invalidation edge-cases for private deployments. need ops buy-in.
miguel: ops notes: cache is doable, we need eviction policy + per-customer TTLs. can be scoped as platform feature with migration path (opt-in). estimate 2 engineers half-sprint + infra config. also need canary gating.
anya: for rollout, require: 1) perf bench (p50/p95 improvement >=20% on target slice), 2) no quality regression on eval set (0.5% metric drift), 3) canary across 5% traffic, 4) docs/opt-in toggle and observability (cache hit rate, eviction rate).
dana: launch criteria from biz side: customer pilot sign-off OR internal SLA test green + pricing note for dedicated customers. also need comms for support.
sara: scope negotiation — engineers prefer starting with the cheap win (KV prefix cache) + observability, then follow with small-batch fast-path if necessary. product asks to reserve runway for B if metrics don't move.
cheng: technical caveat: KV cache helps repeated prefixes (multi-turn chat and system messages). it won't help cold-start single-shot queries. worth adding heuristic routing: if prefix similarity > threshold -> route to cached pool.
miguel: ops-bot: deploy-plan-template created: `/deploys/templates/perf-kv-cache-canary.md` (automated).
anya: i will prepare eval prompts and run baseline tomorrow, then compare with patched runtime. expected turnaround 3 days.
dana: fundraising/customer asks: push to enterprise beta once canary stable. also price impact: minor infra cost increase but should reduce overall token cost via fewer re-computes for multi-turn sessions.
sara: action items: 1) cheng & miguel to scope KV-cache PR + canary plan (due EOD Fri). 2) anya to produce eval set + baseline (3 days). 3) dana to outline pilot/comm and pricing note. i'll compile a one-pager and RICE table after we get numbers.
cheng: ok i'll draft a short spec: what gets cached (prefix length, TTL, invalidation), routing rules, fallback. will share PR link here.
miguel: note for private deployments: include config flags + migrations doc. ops-bot pinned deploy template.
sara: thanks all — this should give us a clear prioritized path (KV-cache first, fallback to fast-path later). i'll add launch criteria to the roadmap item and schedule a 30m sync after we have eval results. :calendar:
